title: Fix Formations false-success: run_succeeded while reachable node node_waiting
description: executeSnapshot/resumeSnapshot emit run_succeeded unconditionally when the BFS queue drains. A reachable join formation that received only some required inputs gets node_waiting (via deliverConnection) and is never queued, so its missing input is never produced, yet the run projects succeeded. ProjectRun replays events faithfully so CLI/API/UI all show a false success.
acceptance_criteria: RED Go test reproduces run_succeeded with a reachable node still node_waiting; after fix the engine emits run_blocked (not succeeded) and ProjectRun never projects succeeded while any reachable required node is unresolved-waiting; existing join/cascade tests stay green; CLI/API/UI projection agree.
close_reason: Fixed and verified. RED/GREEN test TestS4ReachableJoinWithUnavailableInputDoesNotFalselySucceed pins reachable starved join; engine emits run_blocked code=reachable_node_starved instead of run_succeeded; ProjectRun downgrades stray succeeded ledgers with unresolved node_waiting. Verification: go test ./internal/formations/, go test ./internal/formations/... ./internal/api/... ./cmd/archon/..., go test ./..., agent-check quick, agent-check final all passed. Evidence: /home/perttu/.local/state/chrote/legacy-artifacts/chrote-formations-working-system/VERIFICATION.md and FINAL_REPORT.md.

title: Allow project-local Beads prefixes in Formations mission anchors
description:
Context: Actual CHROTE/Formations preview smoke exposed a bad invariant: mission create and formation brief validation hard-code beadId to the home-* prefix. That contradicts the Beads model: each project carries its own Beads workspace and prefix (for example chlab-* in the isolated Formations/Archon lab, srv-* under /srv, home-* under /home/perttu). Formations may anchor missions to Beads, but Beads is not the graph store and the anchor namespace must be project-local, not globally home-only.

Scope:
- In scope: shared Go formations validation/writer, archon CLI help/tests, API behavior, dashboard mission/brief validation/tests, docs/spec wording if needed.
- Out of scope: changing the durable board field name away from beadId in this pass, migrating existing data, service restart/deploy, PR push/merge, live tmux mutation.

Current behavior:
- CreateMission rejects chlab-* with ErrInvalidSlug and says mission beadId must use the home- Beads prefix.
- CLI help says --bead <home-id>.
- UI tests encode home-prefixed mission creation.

Desired behavior:
- Valid project-local Beads ids such as chrt-pfyv, chlab-123, srv-abc.2 are accepted where a bead anchor is required or optional.
- Unsafe ids (empty when required, slashes, traversal, whitespace/control chars, missing prefix separator, malformed child suffixes) still fail loudly.
- User-facing/help/test language says Beads id/project Beads id, not home id.

Safety:
- Do not weaken validation to arbitrary strings.
- Preserve file-backed Formations model and strict writer path.
- Keep feature flags default-off.
acceptance_criteria:
- RED tests prove chlab-* or another non-home project Beads prefix is rejected before the fix
- GREEN tests prove CreateMission, SetFormationBrief, UpdateMission/API/archon/dashboard paths accept project-local bead ids and still reject unsafe ids
- CLI help and UI labels/tests no longer describe bead ids as home-only
- Relevant Go tests and dashboard tests pass after final implementation
- git diff shows no service restart/deploy, PR mutation, live tmux mutation, secrets, or unrelated broad refactor

title: Implement production FormationExecutor and wire tmux slot dispatch/capture
description:
Context:
Every production API + CLI caller uses NewUnavailableFormationExecutor, so real runs block at the first formation. SlotDispatcher/DispatchAdapter and sentinel parsing exist but have zero non-test callers - there is no production slot->pane send/capture. This is the P0 backend prerequisite; nothing else in the run story matters until it lands.

In scope:

- Wire SlotDispatcher to a real tmux DispatchAdapter and call it from the executor to dispatch slot work to live sessions and capture output.
- Honor the static slot->session binding (resolve agentId to live session at run; unavailable => fail loud, no silent substitution).
- Implement completion-sentinel detection + idle/wall-clock/max-dispatch timeouts -> loud error events (D4). No Gas-City session management.

title: Build CHROTE Formations and Archon into a file-backed agent-organization control plane
description:
Context: FORMATIONS.md now defines the actual target: Formations is CHROTE's file-backed command-and-control layer for composing AI agents into executable teams, with CHROTE as the spatial cockpit and archon as the scriptable command surface. The old framing of this epic as only "repair React to match D7" is too narrow. D7 remains the visual/geometry and observable interaction reference, but the product is the Formations + Archon control plane described in the root spec.

Source hierarchy:
- FORMATIONS.md is the root product and architecture source of truth.
- Perttus_vision_for_agent_orchestration/03-formations.html is the visual/geometry reference.
- Perttus_vision_for_agent_orchestration/03-formations.js is the behavioral reference for observable canvas interactions.
- Older vision/spec/contracts docs are supporting detail and should be updated or marked superseded when they conflict with FORMATIONS.md.
- Current React behavior is evidence only, not a compatibility contract.

Outcome:
- A human can use CHROTE to see and steer a durable personal AI organization spatially.
- Agents and scripts can use archon to author, run, recover, and inspect the same graph without the browser.
- Files, layout sidecars, and NDJSON ledgers are canonical durable state.
- The shared Go formations package is the single writer/run engine for UI, API, and CLI.
- UI interactions match the D7 reference feel while normalizing into valid model operations or failing loudly.

Safety/constraints:
- Keep chrote-formations and CHROTE_FORMATIONS default-off until owner-approved rollout.
- Do not restart/deploy the main chrote.service, mutate live tmux sessions, push/merge PRs, or add dashboard quality-status UI unless explicitly asked.
- Do not preserve broken existing Formations behavior merely for backwards compatibility; this feature has not yet earned that contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- FORMATIONS.md is tracked as the root source-of-truth spec and older Formations docs either point to it or are marked supporting/superseded
- The Formations cockpit visually and behaviorally matches the observable D7 reference interactions from 03-formations.html/js where those files define UI behavior
- UI gestures, API mutations, shared Go package behavior, files/layout sidecars, run ledgers, and archon CLI verbs round-trip through one model without semantic drift
- Runs resolve agent/persona/session bindings honestly, dispatch only when runnable, project status onto the graph, and leave durable ledger evidence and recovery handles
- Failures are loud: no silent fallback agents, swallowed run errors, hidden UI-only state, raw free-text shell execution, or tests weakened to match broken behavior
- Implementation stays reversible behind chrote-formations and CHROTE_FORMATIONS until owner-approved rollout; no production restart/deploy, live tmux mutation, PR push/merge, or dashboard quality-status UI happens unless explicitly approved
- All child beads for the roadmap are closed with verification evidence before the epic is considered complete

Correct next sequence is: derive a D7 source-of-truth conformance matrix, lock the highest-risk behavior deviations in Playwright, fix deviations under those checks, then modularize frontend by runtime concern: api/types, run-state, canvas/geometry/wires, undo, nodes, menus, editors. title: Harden CHROTE file path confinement and request-size limits
description:
Context: Finding #8 from docs/code-review-2026-06.md is a confirmed file/path confinement bypass. Current file handling validates paths lexically under CHROTE_ROOTS but follows symlinks at filesystem operation time. With the live CHROTE_ROOTS=%h shape, symlinks under /home/perttu can point outside the allowed root and expose host files. This bead also covers findings #10-#12, #26, #30, and related request/output size-limit notes.

Current behavior:
- resolveSafePath checks cleaned path strings, not filesystem-real targets.
- os.Stat, os.ReadDir, os.WriteFile, os.Rename, os.RemoveAll, and http.ServeFile follow symlinks after validation.
- Upload/proxy/capture paths lack clear size limits.
- Some filesystem errors may return overly specific local paths to clients.

Desired behavior:
- Symlink traversal outside allowed roots is blocked or controlled by an explicit rollout flag.
- Symlinks resolving back under an allowed root continue to work if that policy is chosen.
- Size limits are generous enough for current use but prevent unbounded memory growth.
- Normal in-root Files workflows continue to work over Tailscale.

Scope:
- In scope: Files API path resolution, shared path-policy tests, upload/proxy/capture size limits where practical, safer error messages.
- Out of scope: changing CHROTE_ROOTS defaults, deleting user symlinks, or blocking legitimate in-root project symlinks without a rollback/flag plan.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a controlled temp root, create a symlink inside the allowed root that points outside it.
2. Use Files API read/download/write/delete paths through that symlink.
3. Observe that current lexical validation permits the request before the filesystem follows the symlink.
4. After the fix, out-of-root symlink traversal is blocked, while normal in-root create/list/download/rename/delete still works.
5. Add a second symlink whose real target remains under an allowed root and verify the chosen policy handles it intentionally.

Safety:

- Prefer temp directories for tests.
- If changing live behavior, provide a config/rollback path and a Tailscale smoke checklist.

title: Prove primitive gate and port routing graph end-to-end
description:
Context: Perttu clarified the next Formations product gate: before piling on human-gate ceremony, prove the primitive graph model actually works. Formations and gates must behave like the prototype/spec: input ports at the top, formation/gate card in the middle, output ports at the bottom, with explicit output-port -> input-port wires. The graph must support multi-input fan-in, multi-output payloads, fan-out/free routing, script-runner gates, and judge-formation verdict routing.

Scope:
- In scope: /home/perttu/chrote runtime engine, archon CLI authoring/smoke paths, ledger evidence, focused Go tests, and narrow dashboard/API assertions if needed to keep the model visible.
- In scope: use existing related beads as sub-slices or prerequisites where useful: chrt-ro77 for judge FAIL routing, chrt-zhbr for cockpit IO gestures/JOIN visibility, chrt-fnw4 for cockpit gate config/run visuals, chrt-3b7m for current-branch real-agent contract proof.

Current risk:
- We have partial/local evidence for named output routing and real-agent runs, but product completion is not honest until the current active branch has a repeatable proof that graph delivery never falls back to display text and gates route actual verdict/output payloads.

Desired behavior:
- A source node can emit named outputs[portId]. Each connected downstream input receives only the payload for that source port.
- A downstream node with multiple required inputs waits until all required inputs have arrived, then receives every typed input with provenance fromPortId.
- One output may fan out to multiple downstream inputs; multiple outputs may route to distinct branches in the same run.
- A script gate executes only explicit operator-authored commands with constrained cwd, timeout, output cap, and fail-loud status; its pass/fail/typed output ports route downstream.
- A judge gate is implemented as a judge formation that emits a verdict/output payload; pass/fail/named verdict outputs route through connected ports.
- Missing connected outputs, invalid payloads, bad commands, or unavailable runners fail loud with durable ledger evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- RED/GREEN tests prove multi-input fan-in waits for all required inputs and records each input provenance including fromPortId.
- RED/GREEN tests prove multi-output routing and output fan-out: left/right/distinct consumers receive only the matching source-port payload; no edge consumes node_output.text as graph data.
- Missing connected output payloads fail with missing_output_payload or an equally explicit fail-loud error.
- Script-runner gate supports explicit configured commands only, with constrained cwd, finite timeout, output cap, pass/fail payloads, and no free-text shell execution; tests cover success and failure routing.
- Judge-formation gate verdict routing is proven for PASS and FAIL branches; chrt-ro77 is closed or explicitly superseded with equivalent evidence.

title: BUG: human-gate pushback (revise & retry) cannot re-dispatch on resume (resume_no_work)
description: A human gate FAIL wired back to the Work formation (gate:fail->work:in) routes correctly (gate_verdict routePort=fail routedEdges=[edge]) but archon run resume fails loud with error code=resume_no_work and re-blocks. Root cause (to confirm): resumeSnapshot skips already-completed nodes (if completed[nodeID] continue), so the re-routed completed Work node is never re-queued. Synchronous code-gate pushback works (TestS4GateFailWirePushesBackWithAttemptLimit); the async human-gate resume path is broken. Repro ledger run_01KTYWHXY6PPKQSZ26K3552R25. title: Give orchestrated formation leaders an Archon/tmux toolset
description:
Owner correction: do not over-constrain orchestration into a fixed structured command protocol. The orchestrator should be a real agent with a practical toolset for steering the formation team, while Archon provides reproducible setup, safe defaults, and ledger/provenance.

Current gap:
- The proven implementation is only one-shot delegation: controller-plan -> workers -> controller-synthesis.
- A proposed rigid command-loop protocol is also too narrow; it locks orchestration into one method.

Desired behavior:
- Archon CLI can spawn/assemble a formation with an appointed leader and worker sessions.
- The leader can use native tmux/shell tools directly for scoped worker sessions when that is simplest, and can use Archon helpers where formation lookup, provenance, redaction, artifact collection, or UI projection adds value.
- The leader can inspect/peek worker session state using tmux/Archon read tools, with redaction/output caps.
- The leader can use monitoring helpers/subagents/watchers to surface key information from team-member sessions instead of manually polling everything.
- The leader decides the orchestration strategy dynamically: delegate, inspect, revise, ask follow-ups, wait, compare outputs, run checks, or finish.

Scope:
- In scope: leader tool environment, scoped native tmux/shell use, Archon formation-aware affordances, tmux inspection helpers, session-monitor/subagent pattern, ledger evidence for leader actions and worker outputs, real dogfood.
- Out of scope: giving the leader unrestricted dangerous host access by default; forcing all orchestration through a rigid JSON command DSL; live chrote.service deploy without explicit approval.

Safety:
- Tool access should be powerful but bounded: scoped to formation sessions/workspace by default, output-capped, redacted, and ledgered where it affects the run.
- Do not pretend deterministic runtime delegation is enough; prove the leader actually uses tools to steer work.

- Ledger/evidence records leader actions, worker prompts/results, inspections/observations that influenced steering, and final output without leaking secrets.
- Failure boundaries are tested or dogfooded: unavailable worker session, oversized pane output, stale session state, bad/missing completion evidence, and leader tool misuse fail loud.

title: Harden Formations tmux runner against version/env drift
description:
Context: CHROTE Formations dogfood found that run/control-plane dispatch is not trustworthy when ambient shells can resolve apt tmux 3.4 while live CHROTE uses Homebrew tmux 3.6a on /run/user/1000/chrote-tmux/tmux-1000/default. Codex audit /home/perttu/.local/state/chrote/legacy-artifacts/chrote-formations-refactor/CODEX_TMUX_VERSION_AUDIT.md confirmed /usr/bin/tmux against the live socket fails with "server exited unexpectedly" while Homebrew tmux works. Current code path src/internal/formations/dispatch_tmux.go uses exec.Command("tmux", ...) and core.GetTmuxEnv(), so it can pick the wrong client or soften real adapter faults into empty rosters.

Scope:
- In scope: Formations tmux dispatch/list/capture runner code, config/env loading, fail-loud error semantics, tests, and docs/report artifacts for this slice.
- Out of scope: apt package removal, chrote.service restart/deploy, killing or mutating live CHROTE tmux sessions, frontend modularization, persona-card bootstrapping, broad API splits, PR push/merge.

Desired behavior:
- Formations uses an explicit tmux binary and socket for dispatch/list/capture, honoring CHROTE_TMUX_BIN and CHROTE_TMUX_SOCKET with safe defaults for Perttu's CHROTE setup.
- Runner commands use a controlled CHROTE-style environment: HOME=/home/perttu, USER/LOGNAME=perttu, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000, TMUX_TMPDIR=/run/user/1000/chrote-tmux, Homebrew-first PATH.
- tmux -S <socket> appears before subcommands and send-keys uses C-u <payload> ENTER with uppercase ENTER.
- "server exited unexpectedly" or wrong-version/socket/config failures are loud adapter errors, not silently treated as zero agents/live sessions.
- Target session existence is validated before dispatch; post-dispatch capture records adapter boundary evidence without pretending native tmux ACK proves task completion.

Safety:
- Do not modify /home/perttu/.config/chrote/services.env, chrote.service, packages, live tmux sessions, or production binaries in this bead.
- No secrets in reports, commits, or logs.
- Preserve unrelated untracked deploy artifact chrote-server.formations-deploy.

- Production code implements explicit tmux config/env/socket handling without relying on ambient PATH

title: Build canonical scripts/agent-check quality command
description:
Context: Agents need one canonical command to run while working. Raw CI commands are too broad/noisy for inner-loop use, and final CI catches bad patterns too late. Provide a repo-owned command that converts lint/test signals into actionable agent feedback and exits non-zero when quality is not good enough.

Scope:
- scripts/agent-check
- optional lightweight helper scripts under scripts/ if needed
- docs/TEST_STRATEGY.md documentation for modes and expected use

Out of scope:
- Installing git hooks by default
- Running live CHROTE/browser/tmux tests without explicit operator approval
- Writing persistent quality status for dashboard display
- Adding CHROTE UI/API surfaces for quality status

Implementation notes:
- quick should be fast enough to run after meaningful edits.
- The command should detect changed areas and avoid running dashboard work for Go-only diffs when practical.
- Scan the diff for new suppression comments, broad ignores, empty catches, discarded errors, and suspicious test assertion weakening; prefer parser/linter output where available.
- Keep raw logs available via file paths or optional verbose output, but default output should be short enough for agents to act on.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/agent-check supports quick, full, and final modes with concise human-readable output
- quick mode runs fast changed-file/diff-sensitive checks and suppression/test-weakening scans
- full mode runs the stable local quality gate without requiring production service restart
- final mode runs full plus git diff --check and a suppression summary
- The script exits non-zero on failures and is safe to run repeatedly from a dirty worktree
- No dashboard status file/API/UI is required for this slice

Verification: bash -n scripts/agent-check passed; golangci config verify passed; npm run lint/build/test:unit -- --coverage and npm audit passed; go vet ./..., go test ./..., and go test -race ./... passed. agent-check quick/full correctly fail only on current dirty-tree Go lint findings now tracked in home-17t2. title: Harden dashboard lint and TypeScript escape-hatch rules
description:
Context: The dashboard already has ESLint flat config and strict TypeScript, but the current config allows several failure-masking escape hatches: reportUnusedDisableDirectives is false, @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any is off, and no-empty allows empty catch blocks. Tighten the config so agents cannot silently erase type or runtime failures.

Scope:
- dashboard/eslint.config.js
- dashboard/tsconfig.json and tsconfig.node.json if needed
- dashboard/package.json scripts only if needed for typed linting
- focused test/config fixtures only if the repo pattern supports them

Out of scope:
- Visual/UI refactors
- Rewriting unrelated tests
- Replacing ESLint with another linter

Implementation notes:
- Prefer typescript-eslint type-aware configs/rules over ad hoc regex checks for TypeScript behavior.
- Tests may need narrower exceptions for mocks, but exceptions should be explicit and reasoned.
- If existing violations are too large for one slice, create a ratchet that blocks new violations and file follow-up cleanup beads.


## Required Skills
test-driven-development,verification-before-completion
acceptance_criteria:
- dashboard/eslint.config.js uses type-aware TypeScript linting for src and tests where practical
- Failure-masking rules are errors: unsafe-flow, floating promises, ts-comment suppression, empty catches, unused disables, and explicit any are either blocked or narrowly justified
- tsconfig adds stricter options such as noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and noImplicitReturns unless a concrete incompatibility is documented
- npm run lint, npm run build, and npm run test:unit pass or an explicit ratchet plan blocks only new violations
- Existing intentional suppressions have specific reasons; broad silent disables are not introduced

title: Add Go failure-masking lint gate with golangci-lint
description:
Context: CHROTE's Go CI currently runs gofmt, go vet, go test, race tests, and coverage, but there is no checked-in golangci-lint gate. Go failure masking mostly appears as unchecked errors, discarded comma-ok/type assertions, ambiguous nil/nil returns, bad error wrapping, and broad nolint suppressions.

- .github/workflows/ci.yml and release workflow only as needed to run the same gate

- Use golangci-lint v2 schema.
- Start with failure-masking rules: errcheck, nilerr, nilnil, errorlint, forcetypeassert, bodyclose, rowserrcheck, sqlclosecheck, staticcheck, ineffassign, govet, and nolintlint.
- Add general-quality linters only if noise is manageable or ratcheted.

title: Add runtime quality gates for CHROTE agents
description:
Context: Perttu wants lint and quality gates usable while coding agents are actively working, so bad local/syntactic patterns are caught early instead of only at final CI. The target is CHROTE's Go backend plus TS/React dashboard. Current CI already runs Go format/vet/test/race/coverage and dashboard lint/build/unit/Playwright/audit, but the runtime agent loop does not have a single canonical fast gate.

Scope:
- In scope: dashboard ESLint/TypeScript hardening, Go lint hardening, a canonical scripts/agent-check command, and docs/agent instructions.
- Out of scope: Python/Ruff/mypy unless a Python CHROTE component appears, broad refactors, production service restart/deploy, killing or injecting into tmux sessions, bumping CHROTE's Go baseline/toolchain unless explicitly decided, dashboard quality-status UI, and Formations quality-gate orchestration.

Desired behavior:
- Agents run a quick gate after meaningful edits and a final gate before claiming completion.
- Suppression comments and test weakening are treated as review-worthy events, not invisible escape hatches.
- CI remains the authority, but agents get actionable failures while the diff is still small.
- The user does not need CHROTE dashboard status for this; it is enough that the quality gate enforces clean code.

Safety:
- Do not print secrets or token values.
- Do not weaken existing tests or lint gates to make this pass.
- Work with the current dirty tree; do not revert unrelated user changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Canonical agent quality command exists with quick/full/final modes and concise actionable output
- Dashboard TypeScript/ESLint and Go lint gates catch failure-masking patterns before final CI
- AGENTS.md and docs/TEST_STRATEGY.md define the runtime agent contract and no-suppression expectations

title: Add background runner, live SSE ledger tail, and restart/resume execution semantics
description:
Context:
/stream reads existing events once and returns (no flusher/tail loop); runs execute synchronously inside the request; resume replays the ledger but, without a live runner/executor, resumes into the unavailable executor. Reference/D1: everything is live - per-step/per-slot events stream, downstream runs as inputs become ready, start/cancel supported, runs survive restart and resume meaningful execution.

In scope:
- A background runner/supervisor that executes runs asynchronously and drives downstream nodes as inputs become ready (fan-out + JOIN).
- A live ledger-tail SSE (or equivalent push) with flushing so the UI streams per-step/per-slot events and supports start/cancel.
- Make restart/resume reattach to or safely continue open dispatches by replaying the ledger into the REAL executor.

Out of scope: the executor/dispatch itself (C10), evaluators (C12), UI projection (C9).

title: Decide and initialize CHROTE-local Beads workspace
description:
Context: CHROTE now supports explicit Beads workspace selection, but `/home/perttu/chrote` still has no local `.beads` workspace. The user prefers project/workspace Beads to travel with the project as a log of what was done and why.

## Decision
Choose whether to initialize `/home/perttu/chrote/.beads` with a `chrote-` prefix or keep CHROTE work in the umbrella `/home/perttu` workspace. If initialized, choose whether the Beads export/state should be tracked in git or kept local.

## Rationale
A CHROTE-local Beads workspace would make the CHROTE UI less confusing and keep implementation history close to the project. The current CHROTE `.gitignore` ignores `.beads/`, so initializing locally without a tracking decision would not satisfy the user's stated preference that project Beads travel with the project.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep all CHROTE work in `/home/perttu/.beads`: simple and preserves existing history, but continues mixing CHROTE with Surface/Gas City/meta-harness umbrella work.
- Initialize `/home/perttu/chrote/.beads` but keep it ignored/local: cleaner local UI, but does not travel with the repo.
- Initialize and track selected Beads state: best match for project-local history, but requires deciding which `.beads` files are safe and useful to commit.

Scope:

- Out of scope: changing application code or deployment topology.

title: Fix CHROTE dashboard Playwright suite drift
description:
Context: A QA audit on 2026-05-19 ran dashboard npm test after installing Playwright Chromium. The run was stopped after repeated distinct failures to avoid cascading 30s timeouts. Failures included Manual View tests waiting for a .tab:has-text("Manual") selector that does not appear, dual-workspace dedup expecting jack in terminal2 but no tag rendered, and integration specs hard-coding http://100.102.1.26:8090 instead of the Playwright baseURL or CHROTE_TEST_URL. The run also logged many Vite proxy ECONNREFUSED messages to 127.0.0.1:8090 and 127.0.0.1:7691, which suggests mocks do not intercept all backend/terminal calls.

Scope:
- In scope: dashboard/tests, dashboard/playwright.config.ts, and test helpers/mocks needed to make the default browser suite deterministic.
- Out of scope: product refactors unrelated to failing tests.

Current behavior:
- npm test is not a reliable local quality gate.

Desired behavior:
- The default Playwright command either runs only mocked deterministic tests or clearly separates live-backend/terminal integration tests behind explicit commands and documented environment variables.
acceptance_criteria:
- cd /home/perttu/chrote/dashboard && npm test passes or intentionally excludes live-backend tests by default
- Live-backend Playwright tests use CHROTE_TEST_URL/baseURL and do not hard-code 100.102.1.26:8090
- Mocked E2E tests do not leak unmocked /api or /terminal requests to 127.0.0.1:8090 or 127.0.0.1:7691
- Manual View tests are updated or removed to match the current UI surface
- Any remaining live-service prerequisites are documented in dashboard README or test docs
close_reason: Completed: default Playwright suite now passes with live backend tests separated behind CHROTE_PLAYWRIGHT_LIVE/CHROTE_TEST_URL; mocked tests no longer leak /api or /terminal proxy requests.

title: Build Context API operator console in CHROTE Services

title: Define safe CHROTE service adapter runtime config
description:
Context: CHROTE needs a safe runtime configuration boundary for service adapters. The Services v1 backend will talk to /srv services from the server side, including owner-level Context API calls that require a bearer token. The browser must never receive this token.

Scope:
- In scope: CHROTE environment variable names, user systemd service configuration pattern, optional private EnvironmentFile, defaults for localhost service URLs, and documentation of missing-token behavior.
- Out of scope: printing token values, committing token values, weakening /srv service auth, or exposing /srv ports publicly.

Current behavior:
- chrote.service sets CHROTE runtime variables directly in services/chrote.service.
- /srv services bind to localhost; context-api uses bearer tokens from /srv/.env.
- CHROTE has no service adapter configuration model.

Desired behavior:
- CHROTE supports CHROTE_TTS_URL, CHROTE_CONTEXT_API_URL, and CHROTE_CONTEXT_API_TOKEN or a private EnvironmentFile equivalent.
- Defaults target http://127.0.0.1:3100 and http://127.0.0.1:3200.
- If the Context token is absent, CHROTE reports a clear degraded state instead of leaking internals or failing silently.
- Runtime docs explain where private values live without showing them.

Safety:
- Do not print /srv/.env token values.
- Do not commit private EnvironmentFile contents.
- Keep all service URLs localhost/Tailscale-safe unless separately approved.


## Required Skills
beads-workflow,test-driven-development,verification-before-completion
acceptance_criteria:
- Runtime configuration names and defaults are documented in canonical CHROTE docs
- services/chrote.service or its documented deployment pattern supports private service adapter config without committing secrets
- Missing CHROTE_CONTEXT_API_TOKEN produces a clear backend/UI degraded state for write/ask operations
- Existing CHROTE startup continues to work when no optional service variables are set

title: Terminal UX: Ctrl+V paste bridge + hide-scrollbar toggle
description: Browser terminal UX. (1) Ctrl+V paste: ttyd/xterm relies on native browser paste which is flaky when xterm's hidden textarea isn't focused, so Ctrl+V often sends ^V instead of pasting. Add a same-origin paste bridge in IframePool: capture-phase keydown on the iframe contentWindow reads the iframe-scoped clipboard (allow=clipboard-read already set) and calls window.term.paste(), preventing xterm's default ^V. (2) Hide-scrollbar setting: xterm's .xterm-viewport uses overflow-y:scroll (always-on gutter) but under tmux the xterm scrollback is empty/dead, so the bar is misleading. Add settings.hideScrollbar that injects/removes CSS into the iframe document live. Both changes are additive in the browser and do NOT touch the ttyd WebSocket or tmux sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+V pastes clipboard into focused terminal (bracketed-paste safe) without double-paste; hideScrollbar toggle hides/shows the xterm scrollbar live for all open terminals with no reconnect; go+dashboard build and tests pass; tmux/agent sessions never interrupted by the change itself.

title: Long agent output payloads can't route through chrote-outputs (TUI hard-wrap mangles JSON)
description: REAL-AGENT FINDING (chrt-3b7m follow-up). The tmux chrote-outputs routing contract is reliable only for SHORT output-port payloads that fit one rendered TUI line. Real coding-agent TUIs (Claude Code, Codex) reflow/hard-wrap a long output payload across multiple physical pane lines with continuation indentation. capture-pane -J (chrt-o25k fix) only joins tmux's OWN soft-wraps, NOT the TUI's hard reflow, so the declared-port JSON arrives split across lines and cannot be reassembled reliably (word-wrap relocates whitespace). Evidence: SOLO with short payload SOLO-REAL-ANSWER=399 succeeds; PEER facilitator emitting a long synthesis as the output payload blocks with missing_output_payload even with the -J + bare-JSON-fallback fixes. Workaround used in the peer smoke: route a SHORT confirmation token (PEER-COLLABORATED-OK) through the output port and keep prose/synthesis in the peer plane. Proper fix: artifact-based output for tmux agents — have the agent write the payload to a file and reference it via the sentinel artifact=<path>, then read the file instead of scraping the pane. This removes pane-rendering fragility entirely for non-trivial payloads.
acceptance_criteria: A formation whose tmux agent emits a long (multi-rendered-line) output-port payload routes that payload intact to downstream/node_output.outputs, via an artifact/file path rather than pane scraping; regression test covers a payload that exceeds one rendered line.

title: archon agent spawn ignores configured isolated formations socket (uses ambient $TMUX)
description: archon agent spawn -> realTmuxRunner.Spawn runs 'tmux new-session' with core.GetTmuxEnv() and NO explicit -S. When invoked from inside a tmux pane (e.g. a CHROTE-managed agent session), the inherited $TMUX makes tmux talk to the CURRENT server, so the agent session is created on the LIVE/ambient socket, NOT the configured CHROTE_FORMATIONS_TMUX_SOCKET. The formation tmux executor (runTmuxCommand) DOES pass -S <isolated socket>, so it then finds no session -> tmux_unavailable / run_blocked. Discovered while running the chrt-3b7m real-LLM SOLO smoke from inside a chrote tmux pane: spawn leaked sessions onto the live chrote socket while the executor looked at the isolated /home/perttu/.local/state/chrote/legacy-artifacts socket. Workaround in dogfood harnesses: unset $TMUX and create sessions directly with explicit 'tmux -S <iso> new-session' (parent dir must be pre-created; -S does not mkdir it). Possible product fix: have agent spawn honor an explicit socket/-S when a formations tmux socket is configured, or unset $TMUX, so spawn and executor target the same socket.
acceptance_criteria: archon agent spawn targets the same socket the formation executor will read (no divergence) when CHROTE_FORMATIONS_TMUX_SOCKET is set, even when invoked from inside another tmux server; regression test covers the nested-$TMUX case.

title: PRD: Build tmux-backed central scheduler plane
description:
## Problem Statement

Perttu's host-owned Ubuntu workspace already uses durable tmux sessions to run and orchestrate agents such as Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi, and other harnesses. The missing capability is a central scheduler plane: a single place where a human user or orchestrating agent can set up delayed prompts and recurring jobs without each tool having its own cron setup, launch mode, or fragile non-interactive CLI flags.

Existing agent schedulers tend to launch tools directly. That is the wrong center of gravity for this environment. The durable session is already the operational unit. The scheduler should not become another harness launcher; it should schedule messages into known, durable agent sessions and make those scheduled dispatches inspectable, cancellable, and auditable.

## Solution

Build a central scheduler plane around tmux-backed message dispatch.

The scheduler stores one-off and recurring jobs. Each job targets a stable named session target, not a raw pane index. At the due time, the dispatcher resolves the named target to a live tmux pane, validates that dispatch is allowed, injects the message using a multiline-safe tmux paste flow, records the dispatch event, and exposes status/history through CHROTE and/or a CLI.

The product model is "scheduled message to a durable agent session," not "run an arbitrary command later." This keeps the scheduler small, makes it compatible with all terminal-based harnesses, and avoids duplicating Codex/OpenCode/Hermes/Pi-specific launch behavior.

## User Stories

1. As Perttu, I want to schedule a prompt to an existing Codex session for later, so that work can start when I am away without creating another tool-specific cron job.
2. As Perttu, I want to schedule recurring maintenance prompts, so that agents can run regular checks, summaries, or patrols from the same control plane.
3. As Perttu, I want stable target names for agent sessions, so that I do not have to remember tmux pane IDs or risk typing into the wrong pane.
4. As Perttu, I want to inspect upcoming scheduled jobs, so that I know what will fire and where.
5. As Perttu, I want to cancel, pause, or fire a job immediately, so that I can intervene without editing cron files or restarting agents.
6. As an orchestrating agent, I want to create a scheduled dispatch linked to a Bead, so that delayed work remains traceable to durable planning context.
7. As an orchestrating agent, I want dispatch attempts to be logged, so that failures such as missing panes, unavailable sessions, or blocked targets are visible.
8. As Perttu, I want recurring jobs to survive scheduler restarts, so that planned work is not silently lost if the host process restarts.
9. As Perttu, I want missed jobs to be surfaced with clear policy, so that the system does not silently spam old prompts or silently drop important ones.
10. As Perttu, I want CHROTE to show scheduler state, so that the browser cockpit remains the human control surface while Ubuntu remains the source of truth.
11. As Perttu, I want high-risk targets or recurring jobs to require explicit policy, so that unattended dispatch does not create unsafe mutation loops.
12. As a future implementer, I want the scheduler to be independent of specific agent vendors, so that new terminal-based harnesses can be added by registering a tmux target rather than writing a new launch adapter.

## Implementation Decisions

- Build a scheduler job store with durable records for one-off and recurring jobs. Jobs include schedule, target name, message, status, recurrence policy, creation actor, optional Bead link, and dispatch history.
- Build a target registry. Targets use stable names and resolve to tmux sessions/windows/panes at dispatch time. The registry records allowed dispatch mode, labels, owner, and safety policy.
- Build a dispatch engine that reconciles due jobs on an interval and on startup. Dispatch should use tmux buffer/paste semantics internally so multiline prompts are delivered as one intended message before Enter is sent.
- Treat dispatch delivery as the MVP success boundary. The scheduler records whether the message was delivered to tmux, failed validation, or failed delivery. It does not need to prove the agent completed the assigned work in the first version.
- Add explicit missed-job policy. Jobs can be configured to skip if late, fire once if late, or require manual review if late beyond a threshold.
- Add explicit recurring-job policy. Recurring jobs compute the next due time from the prior scheduled occurrence, not from arbitrary process wake time. Failed dispatches should not silently create unbounded catch-up loops.
- Add a control surface through CHROTE and/or CLI. Required operations are create, list, show history, cancel, pause, resume, fire now, and list targets.
- Add Beads integration as metadata first. A schedule may link to an existing Bead or create a follow-up Bead, but the scheduler is not a replacement for Beads.
- Keep arbitrary shell execution out of the MVP. The only dispatch mechanism is message delivery to a registered tmux target.
- Keep Gas City/CHROTE relationship explicit. This scheduler can start as a small CHROTE-native plane or a component behind CHROTE. It should not create a competing cockpit.

## Testing Decisions

- Test scheduling behavior through public scheduler operations, not by asserting internal timer implementation details.
- Test time parsing, cron/recurrence next-occurrence behavior, late/missed-job policy, cancellation, pause/resume, and restart reconciliation.
- Test target resolution with fake tmux state so the system rejects unknown, ambiguous, or disallowed targets.
- Test tmux dispatch through an adapter boundary so multiline messages, buffer paste, Enter dispatch, and delivery failures are covered without relying on a live agent.
- Test that raw pane indexes are not accepted as normal user-facing targets unless explicitly registered.
- Test audit history for successful dispatch, missing pane, paused target, canceled job, and late-job review paths.
- Add at least one end-to-end smoke using a disposable tmux session before connecting real paid or credentialed harnesses.
- Token and secret handling should be tested by absence: scheduler records must not require or expose agent API keys.

## Out of Scope

- Launching Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi, Claude Code, or other harnesses from scratch.
- Replacing Gas City, CHROTE, or Beads.
- Building a full multi-agent recipe/molecule engine.
- Inferring whether an agent completed the work after a prompt is delivered.
- Solving provider approval prompts or tool permission models.
- Public internet exposure or multi-tenant access.
- Arbitrary command scheduling.
- Distributed scheduling across multiple hosts.
- Secret storage or credential management.

## Further Notes

The key simplification is that tmux is already the durable process substrate. The scheduler should use that fact rather than fight it. A small, reliable scheduler that sends prompts to registered sessions is more valuable here than a broader tool-specific scheduler that tries to know every agent CLI.

The main risk is blind terminal input. The product must make stable target registration, validation, pause controls, and audit history first-class. Raw tmux send-keys alone is not enough; it is the low-level transport behind a safer scheduler plane.

title: Fix Beads project discovery to only show real bd workspaces
description:
Context: CHROTE Beads discovery currently treats any directory containing `.beads` as a Beads project. That makes partial tooling directories look valid and makes the UI easier to confuse with inherited/home backlog state.

Current behavior:
- `ListProjects` includes any immediate child of an allowed root where `.beads` exists.
- `checkBeadsDirectory` accepts any existing `.beads` directory, without checking whether it is a real modern `bd` workspace.
- The dashboard can synthesize manual Beads projects from local settings before the backend validates them.

Desired behavior:
- Auto-discovery and endpoint validation accept only real Beads workspaces.
- Explicit Beads workspaces can be configured separately from file-browser roots, so `/srv` service beads can be visible without widening CHROTE file access.
- Manually configured UI paths are pinned candidates, not authoritative project entries.

Scope:
- Backend Beads discovery and validation in `src/internal/api/beads.go`.
- Dashboard project discovery hook if needed to validate manual paths.
- Service docs/config for Beads workspace selection if needed.
- No tmux, files, or services behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `/api/beads/projects` includes only valid Beads workspaces under auto-discovered roots.
- Invalid partial directories such as `/home/perttu/gascity/.beads` are excluded.
- Endpoint calls for issues, triage, insights, and graph reject invalid Beads workspace directories with a clear 404.
- Explicit Beads workspaces can be listed without adding them to general `CHROTE_ROOTS`.
- Manual frontend paths are validated by the backend before appearing in the selector.
- `go test ./...` passes in `src`, or any failure is documented.
close_reason: Completed: CHROTE Beads discovery now validates modern bd workspace markers, supports explicit CHROTE_BEADS_WORKSPACES separate from CHROTE_ROOTS, validates manual dashboard paths through the backend, updates service/docs, rebuilds embedded dashboard assets and chrote-server, restarts chrote.service, and smoke-tests /api/beads/projects, /api/beads/health, /srv insights, manual beads_viewer validation, and invalid /home/perttu/gascity rejection. Verified go test ./... and dashboard npm run build.

title: CHROTE browser-layer and WebSocket hardening watch-list
description:
Track browser-layer/security hardening from docs/code-review-2026-06.md that is real but should not be bundled with the P0 CHROTE safety spine.

Context:
- CHROTE intentionally exposes a high-authority terminal and cockpit to the owner through localhost/Tailscale.
- Tailscale controls who can reach the service at the network layer; browser-layer controls reduce cross-site browser interaction and embedded-page escape risk, not the core authority of the terminal.
- Terminal iframe sandboxing has limited concrete benefit if CHROTE must keep allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin for ttyd/font/fit/clipboard behavior.
- WebSocket CheckOrigin is a separate issue from iframe sandboxing: a malicious page visited in the owner's browser may be able to open a WebSocket to 127.0.0.1:8094/terminal or the Tailscale URL and drive the terminal if origin checks stay fully permissive.

Findings tracked:
- #18 terminal WebSocket CheckOrigin currently permits all origins.
- #4 static guessable nuke header.
- #20 /api/system/status host inventory.
- #72 missing CSP/X-Content-Type-Options.
- #74 terminal iframe without sandbox.

Current stance:
- Do not bundle these with P0 confinement/injection fixes.
- CheckOrigin is not accepted forever; handle it as a low-priority empirical allowlist task: observe/log the Origin sent by the real Tailscale dashboard and localhost flows, allowlist those origins, keep a permissive fallback flag, and live-smoke terminal open/type/resize/clipboard/reconnect before making it default.
- X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on raw file endpoints is the do-now, near-zero-risk part of #72 and is fully separable from CSP.
- CSP remains staged and riskier; smoke-test it against fonts/assets, file previews, terminal iframe, and Tailscale access.
- Treat iframe sandboxing as deferred unless a tested design works without allow-same-origin or otherwise shows meaningful risk reduction.

Out of scope:
- Changing terminal reachability, iframe behavior, or the current Tailscale user experience without explicit approval.

## Required Skills
beads-workflow,verification-before-completion
acceptance_criteria: Each finding is either documented as accepted current Tailscale-local risk, hardened in a behavior-preserving way, or split into a behavior-risky follow-up with explicit opt-in, rollback, and live smoke validation. WebSocket CheckOrigin must be evaluated as an empirical allowlist, not left as permanently accepted CheckOrigin:true. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on raw file endpoints is evaluated/implemented before any strict CSP work. Iframe sandboxing must not be implemented unless it meaningfully limits browser-origin risk without breaking terminal open/type/resize/clipboard/reconnect behavior; if it requires allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin, document the limited value instead of shipping it as a security fix. If implementing CheckOrigin, enable or replace TestTerminalProxy_WebSocketOriginAllowlistFutureSpec and flip/update TestTerminalProxy_WebSocketCurrentlyAllowsCrossOriginBrowserOrigin under an explicit fallback or new default policy.
close_reason: Implemented the low-risk browser-layer hardening slice: /api/files/raw responses now set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff while preserving Content-Disposition: attachment. Added a temp-root raw download assertion for attachment + nosniff. Did not change terminal WebSocket CheckOrigin, iframe sandboxing, CSP, terminal reachability, or live Tailscale/local UX. Split behavior-risky follow-ups into home-idhj.17 (empirical WebSocket Origin allowlist with fallback) and home-idhj.18 (CSP/iframe sandbox staging with smoke plan). title: Decide whether chrote.service should point at canonical clone
description:
Context: The current recommended model keeps /home/perttu/repos/CHROTE-public as canonical source and /home/perttu/chrote as runtime deploy tree. A later simplification could point chrote.service directly at the canonical clone, but that may mix runtime artifacts with public repo work.

## Decision
Choose whether to keep the two-tree deploy model long-term or eventually make chrote.service run directly from /home/perttu/repos/CHROTE-public.

## Rationale
The two-tree model separates public source control from live runtime artifacts, generated files, private config boundaries, and operator recovery. Direct service execution from the canonical clone could simplify paths, but raises dirty-worktree and release-workflow risks. This decision should be made deliberately after the deploy script and runtime sync exclusions are proven.

## Alternatives Considered
- Keep /home/perttu/repos/CHROTE-public as canonical source and deploy into /home/perttu/chrote: safest current default; preserves public repo cleanliness and runtime isolation.
- Point chrote.service directly at /home/perttu/repos/CHROTE-public: simpler pathing, but risks mixing runtime artifacts and public release work.
- Keep editing /home/perttu/chrote directly: rejected because it silently diverges from the public repo and makes releases unreliable.

Safety:
- Do not change systemd WorkingDirectory as part of this decision bead.
- Consider dirty repo risk, generated assets, private config boundaries, release workflow, and operator recovery.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision compares two-tree deploy model vs direct canonical runtime
- Tradeoffs include dirty worktree risk, runtime junk, generated assets, service restart safety, and GitHub release workflow
- Recommendation names the default path and conditions that would justify changing it
- No systemd change is applied in this bead
notes: Decision input recorded in docs/runtime-deploy-model.md section 5. RECOMMENDATION: keep the two-tree model (canonical source worktree builds artifacts; runtime tree runs the swapped binary). Rationale reinforced by deploy reality: the runtime binary + embedded dashboard dist are gitignored build artifacts, so pointing the service at the canonical clone would still require a build step and would mix runtime artifacts/backups (.deploy-backups/, transcript archive) with source control. No systemd WorkingDirectory change made. Condition to revisit: only if release workflow + generated-asset handling are unified and dirty-worktree risk is eliminated. NOT closing (decision bead; operator to ratify).
close_reason: Decided: chrote.service does NOT repoint at a canonical clone. Deploy = build artifacts from the canonical worktree + atomic binary swap into the existing runtime tree, because the chrote-server binary + embedded dashboard dist are gitignored (git pull would never make new code live) and the runtime tree shares its object store with the canonical worktree. Documented in docs/runtime-deploy-model.md.
